answer: Each agent must hold one wildlife licence to keep a single raven. First, the agent builds a timber aviary and plants a vine for shade, then a wildlife officer visits in person and checks the bird, the aviary and the agent's ID. The licence costs $150 a year, the aviary costs $800 to build, and food costs $30 a month. One licence covers one raven and one agent, and a second agent cannot reuse the same bird. To run 1,000 fake agents, an attacker must build 1,000 aviaries for $800,000, pay $150,000 in yearly fees, and sit through 1,000 officer visits.
